data.title: Was the Fed’s hike one-and-done? Analysts weigh what comes next
data.description:
The Federal Reserve delivered its first rate hike since July 2023 on Wednesday, lifting the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4% in a unanimous 12-0 decision.

The move was broadly expected. What investors are now trying to determine is whether the increase marks the beginning of a new tightening cycle or ultimately proves to be a one-off move as inflation and growth data evolve.

The Fed's latest projections lean toward another increase. Sixteen of 18 officials see at least one more hike this year.

But the market response has already shown that the debate is not simply about the 25 basis points.

Stocks fell after the decision and Warsh's press conference on Wednesday, with the Dow dropping 1.21% and the S&P 500 losing 0.45%.

The two-year Treasury yield rose to 4.738%, while the 10-year yield reached 5% and the dollar strengthened.

By Thursday, much of the equity selloff had reversed.

The Dow rose 0.62%, the S&P 500 gained 1.14%, and the Nasdaq jumped 1.69%, led by technology stocks. The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.939%.

That quick reversal has left investors focused on the next question: does the Fed actually need to hike again?

Warsh makes inflation the test

Warsh's message after the decision was firmly centered on inflation.

The Fed's statement said economic activity was expanding at a solid pace, domestic spending remained resilient, productivity growth was strong, and capital investment was robust.

It also said inflation remained elevated and that the rate increase would support a timelier return to the central bank's 2% goal.

That combination matters for the next move. The Fed is facing inflation that remains above target while the economy has not yet weakened enough to force policymakers to prioritize growth.

Robert R. Johnson, professor of finance at Creighton University's Heider College of Business, sees the move as the start of further tightening.

“This is unlikely to be a one-and-done move. This is likely the start of further tightening,” Johnson told Invezz.

He points to the futures market, which he said was assigning a 55% probability to another 25-basis-point increase after the October meeting.

Johnson's broader argument is that inflation remains the central problem for policymakers while the labor market and wider economy have remained comparatively resilient.

“To paraphrase James Carville, ‘it’s inflation, stupid!’” Johnson said.

“The economy has been very resilient, and employment is a much less of an issue than inflation.”

Eugenia Mykuliak, founder of B2PRIME Group, reached a similar conclusion after Warsh's remarks.

“I believe the Fed chair was clear in these statements, namely in the fact that the inflation is too high and for too long,” Mykuliak told Invezz.

“Now I’m sure there will be another rate hike for sure.”

That is also reflected in the Fed's projections.

While Warsh again did not submit an individual projection, only two of the 18 submitted rate paths showed no further increase this year.

Inflation may not be a problem rates can solve alone

That creates the central complication in the one-and-done debate: not all of the current inflation pressure is being generated by excess demand.

J.D. Pisula, CEO of Accolade Advisory and a former bond fund manager, said the central bank has limited ability to address inflation caused by supply shocks.

“There is some risk that the Fed might negatively impact aggregate demand in the economy when the real issue is the supply shock driven by the war with Iran,” Pisula told Invezz.

The Fed, he said, “only controls one policy lever” and cannot directly control inflation caused by fiscal policy or global supply shocks.

That matters because energy prices remain an important source of uncertainty.

A persistent oil shock could keep inflation elevated even as tighter monetary policy slows interest-sensitive parts of the economy.

The issue is also highlighted by Morgan Stanley's post-decision assessment.

Chief US economist Michael Gapen said policymakers are likely thinking about more than one move because monetary policy works with a lag.

A 25-basis-point increase, he argued, would not fundamentally alter the macroeconomic outlook by itself.

But Gapen also outlined a route to a very different outcome.

If inflation continues to moderate, he said, the Fed could intend to hike again but find that the incoming data no longer justify it.

In that case, September could become an “ex-post one and done” move even though policymakers did not enter the meeting expecting it to be the last increase.

That distinction is central to the debate.

The question is not necessarily whether the Fed intends to hike again.

It is whether the data between now and the next meeting remain strong enough to make another increase necessary.

The one-and-done case is still alive

ING is making that case explicitly.

In its September 17 assessment, ING acknowledged that the Fed's own projections include another hike but maintained its view that September could ultimately be a one-off.

The bank points to weaker underlying labor-market trends, 3% wage growth, moderating shelter inflation and tariff-related price pressures that are increasingly incorporated.

Energy is the key variable.

ING expects oil and gas flows from the Persian Gulf to improve, allowing energy prices to resume their decline later in the year and helping inflation move lower.

If that happens alongside continued labor-market softness, the case for another hike would weaken.

ING compares the setup with the late 1990s, when Alan Greenspan's Fed delivered a one-off “risk management” hike in 1997 before a prolonged pause.

The bond market, however, remains a source of caution.

ING said the 25bp increase had limited impact on the long end immediately after the decision but maintained a bearish stance on long-term Treasuries.

It expects the 10-year yield to move back above 5% and sees 5.25%-5.5% as attainable if inflation, fiscal deficits, issuance and AI-related investment continue to pressure longer-dated yields.

That means even a one-and-done Fed may not automatically translate into lower borrowing costs across the economy.

Markets absorb the initial shock

The first market reaction to the hike was consistent with a more hawkish policy signal.

The two-year Treasury yield, which is more closely tied to expectations for the Fed's policy rate, jumped after the decision.

Longer-term yields were initially more contained, leaving the curve flatter. The dollar also strengthened.

But Thursday's rebound suggested investors were able to look past the immediate policy shock.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq both advanced more than 1%, with technology stocks leading the move, while the 10-year yield pulled back below 5%.

Easing oil prices, lower Treasury yields, and solid labor-market data helped stocks recover.

Evan Mills, a financial adviser at Scholar Advising, argues that the market is responding more to the Fed's message than the size of the move.

“The hike was the headline, but the message was tightening,” Mills told Invezz.

Mills expects another rate increase to have its clearest effect at the front end of the Treasury curve, particularly the two-year note.

Longer-term yields, he said, are more complicated because they reflect expectations for future growth, demand and inflation as well as current monetary policy.

The equity implications are also uneven. Mills said expensive growth stocks and highly leveraged companies are more exposed to higher rates because of the effect on discount rates and financing costs.

But he sees a limit to that pressure.

“I still think stocks can handle one more rate hike better than they can handle the return of the inflation problem,” Mills said.

Tim Thomas, CFA, CIO and wealth manager at Seattle-based Badgley Phelps Wealth Managers, takes a similar view that a limited tightening cycle need not derail equities.

“We are not too concerned about a couple of 25-basis-point rate increases given the strength in the economy and the tremendous growth in corporate earnings,” Thomas told Invezz.

“If monetary policy tightening is relatively modest, we expect the growth in earnings and the economy to be the primary drivers of equity prices, sustaining the bull market.”

Thomas expects the Fed to avoid an extended series of increases, although he said markets could face a period of choppier trading along the way.

The data now decide

For now, the Fed has left both possibilities open.

Its projections clearly lean toward another hike, with 16 of 18 officials expecting at least one more increase this year.

Inflation forecasts were also revised higher, while the median 2026 PCE inflation forecast rose to 3.7% from 3.6% in June.

At the same time, the unemployment projection was lowered to 4.1% from 4.3%, and the growth forecast was nudged higher.

Those numbers make another hike easier to justify if inflation stays elevated.

But ING and Morgan Stanley highlight the other side of the equation: monetary policy operates with a lag, labor-market weakness may be greater than the unemployment rate suggests, and some inflation pressures could ease without additional tightening.

The market reaction has so far reflected that uncertainty.

Wednesday's selloff showed the cost of the Fed's hawkish message; Thursday's rebound showed that investors were not treating the decision as the beginning of an inevitable prolonged tightening cycle.

The next few inflation and employment reports will therefore matter more than the September decision itself.

The Fed has shown that it is willing to tighten again. Whether it actually does so will depend on whether inflation remains stubborn enough, and economic growth resilient enough, to make another hike necessary.

The post Was the Fed’s hike one-and-done? Analysts weigh what comes next appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Evening digest: Aramco to halt Europe oil deliveries, Bitcoin hits $81K
data.description:
Saudi Aramco has told at least two European refining customers they will receive no crude oil in October following damage to the kingdom’s key East-West pipeline, while gold prices rose and oil prices eased as investors assessed the latest developments in the Middle East.

At the same time, Bitcoin jumped 6% on September 18, briefly moving above $81,000 after trading around $77,000-$78,000 for most of the week, with the cryptocurrency also benefiting from the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s new framework for tokenized stocks.

Saudi Aramco halts oil deliveries to Europe

Saudi Aramco has informed at least two European refining customers that they will receive no crude deliveries next month after an attack damaged Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline, Bloomberg reported.

European refiners normally receive Saudi crude under term contracts that provide regular monthly supplies, but the reported decision means those deliveries will not take place in October and applies to European buyers, according to the report.

The 1,200-kilometre East-West pipeline can transport up to 7 million barrels of oil per day from Saudi Arabia’s eastern oil fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu.

The pipeline has been shut since a September 10 drone attack damaged pumping infrastructure.

Reuters reported that three pumping stations were damaged, one more than initially assessed.

Saudi Arabia is seeking to restore about half of the pipeline’s capacity within days, although estimates for a full recovery range from several weeks to longer.

European refiners are seeking alternative supplies from the North Sea and other sources.

Poland’s Orlen, which relies on Saudi Arabia for around 40% of the crude feedstock across its three refineries, has issued more than 10 tenders since last Friday for alternative supplies.

Gold prices rebound

Gold prices rose to a one-week high on Friday as easing oil prices reduced some concerns about prolonged inflationary pressure, with spot gold up 0.88% at $4,378.49 an ounce.

US gold futures settled 0.45% higher at $4,419.40, while silver rose 2.3% to $66.70, platinum gained 2.2% to $1,812.50 and palladium increased 1.5% to $1,310.20.

Gold's gains came despite a stronger dollar and higher US interest rates, which can reduce the appeal of non-yielding assets.

The Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4% on Wednesday, while traders saw a 55% chance of another hike in October.

Oil prices retreat

Brent crude fell 1.56% to $103.19 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate declined 2.17% to $99.7 as concerns about Saudi supply disruptions eased.

Saudi Arabia has been working to reroute some crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz, while China reportedly asked Iran to limit attacks by Houthi rebels on Saudi oil infrastructure.

However, the physical oil market remains tight, with some European crude cargoes trading above $130 a barrel and North Sea Forties reaching $136.75.

The Strait of Hormuz also remained largely disrupted, with only four commodities vessels passing through on Thursday compared with a 10-day average of about 16, according to preliminary shipping data.

Bitcoin breaks above $81,000

Bitcoin jumped 6% on September 18, crossing $81,000 after spending most of the week between $77,000 and $78,000.

The move followed the SEC’s September 17 announcement of a five-year exemption allowing certain platforms to facilitate on-chain trading of tokenized stocks.

The exemption provides a regulatory pathway for eligible platforms to offer blockchain-based versions of traditional equities, with tokenized securities required to provide holders with the same rights and privileges as equivalent traditional shares.

The Bitcoin rally also came as oil prices pulled back, easing some of the inflation concerns that had weighed on risk assets.

The move followed the Senate’s failure earlier in the week to advance the CLARITY Act, which would have established a broader regulatory framework for digital assets.

The post Evening digest: Aramco to halt Europe oil deliveries, Bitcoin hits $81K appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Micron stock rises as RBC sees AI memory demand supporting valuation
data.description:
Micron Technology (MU) shares rose on Friday as RBC Capital Markets said the memory-chip maker's valuation does not fully reflect its exposure to the artificial intelligence-driven memory boom.

Micron stock gained as much as 3.12%. RBC analyst Srini Pajjuri reiterated an Outperform rating and a $1,500 price target.

Pajjuri pointed to rising memory requirements from AI workloads, including the shift towards more memory-intensive agentic AI applications.

AI demand keeps memory supply tight

RBC said memory demand continues to exceed available supply, with several structural constraints contributing to the imbalance.

These include rapid growth in high-bandwidth memory (HBM), limited clean-room capacity and tight availability of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) equipment.

HBM has become increasingly important for AI accelerators because it can provide high memory bandwidth for demanding AI workloads.

The expansion of agentic AI could further increase memory requirements as AI systems become capable of operating with greater autonomy and handling multiple tasks.

A Seeking Alpha report also argued that AI is changing the historical cyclicality of memory demand.

Memory consumption has traditionally been driven by equipment volumes and increasing memory content per device, making the industry sensitive to hardware replacement cycles.

However, Micron's margins have shown a prominent upward trend since 2022, while the company has also repeatedly exceeded market expectations in recent quarters.

Micron is scheduled to report its next results on September 30.

Valuation leaves room for expansion

Despite the tight supply-demand environment, RBC said Micron's valuation remains relatively modest.

According to Pajjuri, Micron trades at approximately 6.5 times expected forward earnings. He said this valuation gives limited credit to the company's Strategic Customer Agreements and floor pricing agreements.

RBC believes the combination of sustained AI demand, structural supply constraints, and customer agreements could support an expansion in Micron's valuation multiple.

Long-term contracts are becoming increasingly important in the memory industry.

Micron and its peers are securing agreements that establish future purchasing commitments for DRAM and NAND products.

These arrangements can provide greater visibility into future demand while reflecting the tight conditions across the memory market.

Capacity constraints support memory prices

The memory industry's supply response is constrained by the time required to expand physical capacity.

New facilities require construction, equipment installation, qualification, and increases in production throughput, which can extend the period before additional supply becomes available.

There is also high barriers to entry and a relatively small number of competitors with global scale and experience through previous industry downturns.

Capital allocation decisions have increasingly been driven by expected returns rather than attempts to gain market share through higher production volumes.

This dynamic has contributed to a gap between memory supply and demand and supported higher memory prices.

AI workloads could add another structural source of demand as larger models, wider context windows and more advanced reasoning capabilities require greater memory capacity.

For Micron, the combination of AI-driven consumption, tight industry capacity and longer-term customer agreements remains central to the outlook ahead of its September 30 earnings report.

data.title: BitMine stock is stuck in neutral: here’s why it is about to pump hard
data.description:
BitMine stock has held steady above a crucial support level as the company nears an inflection point in its Ethereum accumulation strategy. BMNR rose to $25.58, up by nearly 100% from its lowest level this year. This rally may continue after it formed a highly bullish chart pattern and as Ether steadies. 

BitMine stock rises as Ethereum rally continues

ETH token jumped and crossed the important resistance level of $2,500. It was trading at $2,595, up sharply from the year-to-date low of $1,517. This rally coincided with the broader crypto market gains, that pushed the market capitalization of all coins up by over 4% to $2.75 trillion. Bitcoin also jumped above the crucial resistance level of $80,000.

BitMine is one of the top beneficiaries of Ethereum’s surge because of its large holdings. It now holds 5.956 million coins, currently valued at over $15.4 billion. 

There are signs that ETH price will continue doing well this year. As the chart below shows, the token has formed a bullish flag pattern and is now slowly nearing its upper side. This pattern is made up of a vertical line and a horizontal channel.

In addition to a bullish flag pattern, the token has slowly formed a golden cross pattern, which is made up of a 200-day and 50-day moving average crossover. It usually leads to more gains by confirming that the short-term momentum is accelerating.

Therefore, there is a possibility that it will jump to $3,000, which is about 16% above the current level. 

ETH price chart | Source: TradingView

Transition from cash burn to cash flow

BitMine stock is rising as the company remains in a transition period. After spending 15 months in an Ethereum accumulation phase, the company is now moving towards cash generation and strategic initiatives. 

Unlike BitMine and other crypto treasury companies, Tom Lee has a strategy of owning just 5% of all ETH tokens in circulation. The estimated amount is 6 million tokens, meaning that he now needs to buy just 43,000. If the recent trend continues, chances are that the company completed the accumulation this week. Alternatively, it may complete the process next week.

After this, the company, which has about 3 employees, will transition from dilution into focusing on free cash flow (FCF). It will do that by staking its tokens through MAVAN, the validator network it built recently. With the staking yield being about 2.7%, it means that the company will generate about 162k ETH coins a year. 

The value of these coins will depend on the prevailing Ethereum price, and the company will be able to use these funds to repurchase shares, pay dividends, and make strategic investments. This explains why Cantor Fitzgerald recently boosted its target for the stock to $60.

BMNR stock price technical analysis

BitMines stock chart | Source: TradingView

Technicals suggest that the BMNR stock has more room to run in the coming weeks. It remains above the important support level of $23.67, its highest point in March, April, and May this year. 

The stock has formed a bullish flag pattern, a common bullish reversal sign in technical analysis. It is also about to form a golden cross pattern as the spread between the 50-day and 200-day moving averages narrows. These patterns suggest that the stock may rebound and possibly hit the key resistance level of $40 soon.

The post BitMine stock is stuck in neutral: here’s why it is about to pump hard appeared first on Invezz

data.title: BMO recommends betting on a recovery in this semiconductor stock
data.description:
MACOM Technology (MTSI) stock is inching higher on Friday after a senior BMO Capital analyst – Harsh Kumar – issued a bullish note in favour of the semiconductor firm.

In his research note, Kumar upgraded MTSI to Outperform and reiterated his $335 price objective, which signals potential upside of about 23% from current levels.

BMO’s bullish call brings much-needed reprieve to MACOM shares that are currently down some 30% versus their year-to-date high.

Why is BMO Capital bullish on MACOM stock

BMO highlights that the recent pullback presents an attractive entry point, as MTSI stock’s forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple compressed sharply from the high-50s in June down to about 29x.

More importantly, “fundamentals have remained rather solid throughout, driven by data center and industrial/defense," he added.

A major catalyst lies within the hyper-scaler buildout: massive capex from cloud service providers and artificial intelligence (AI) labs powering next-gen compute and networking infrastructure.

This is, in fact, expected to result in a 70% increase in MACOM’s data center vertical in 2026, an impressive acceleration from the 47% growth recorded in the prior fiscal year.

On Friday, the semiconductor stock broke above its 20-day moving average (MA), indicating the upward momentum could sustain in the near-term.

What else could drive MTSI shares higher?

Beyond cloud datacenters, MACOM shares are attractive because the firm’s broad-based portfolio is finding significant momentum in specialized industrial and defense applications.

According to the BMO analyst, defense demand “remains resilient and space becomes a material contributor to growth next year.”

With its advanced high-performance analog and RF products, MTSI is expanding its market share across satellite communication, radar, and next-gen telecom hardware.

Investors should also note that the semiconductor stock has a history of closing both October and November in “green” – a seasonal pattern that further improves its near-term appeal.

How Wall Street recommends playing MACOM

BMO’s constructive call mirrors broader sentiment across Wall Street, where institutional backing remains overwhelmingly positive.

LSEG data reveals that out of 19 analysts actively tracking MTSI shares, 15 maintain either a Buy or Strong Buy recommendation, with the remaining four assigning a Hold rating. None recommend selling.

With the mean Street price target currently hovering around $395, the broader consensus agrees that MACOM’s continued decline of about 30% from its late-May record high of $418.90 offers an attractive entry point if you’re interested in holding it for the longer term.

Supported by the strong fiscal fourth quarter (Q4) earnings outlook and robust institutional ownership above 76%, the stock appears strongly positioned to turn its recent operational momentum into an extended market recovery through the remainder of this year.

That said, MACOM Technology Solutions Holdings Inc does not currently pay a dividend, which makes it rather unattractive for income-focused investors in 2026.

The post BMO recommends betting on a recovery in this semiconductor stock appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Trump-Xi summit: What to expect on tariffs, Taiwan, Iran and AI
data.description:
Donald Trump is set to welcome Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House next week for their second meeting this year, with the two leaders seeking to stabilise a relationship strained by trade disputes, tensions over Taiwan and Iran, and a growing rivalry over artificial intelligence.

Xi’s visit, expected on Sept. 24, will be his first to the White House in a decade and the first Chinese state visit to the United States since 2015, when he was received by then-President Barack Obama.

The summit comes at a politically consequential moment for Trump.

The US president is grappling with the Iran war, rising prices and declining popularity ahead of November’s midterm congressional elections, increasing the importance of any economic or diplomatic gains he can bring home from talks with Xi.

For China, the meeting comes as its economy remains heavily dependent on exports, with the country on track to record a trade surplus of about $1 trillion for a second consecutive year.

Beijing is likely to focus on securing access to US technology and maintaining stable trade relations while pressing Washington on Taiwan and other strategic issues.

Markets will be watching closely for signs that the two countries can extend a tariff truce that helped prevent another escalation of their trade war.

Trade truce and tariff negotiations

The October summit in South Korea produced a tariff truce that paused a confrontation in which tariffs imposed by the world's two largest economies had threatened to disrupt global supply chains.

That agreement is due to expire on November 10.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said this month that the two countries would make "some announcements on agriculture and non-tariff barriers".

Investors will also be looking for progress on an agreed mutual tariff reduction covering $30 billion in goods, Reuters reported.

Bloomberg reported on Tuesday that energy tariffs could be included in the $30 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts flagged after the May summit but yet to be implemented.

Such a move could pave the way for Chinese imports of US LNG to resume, with annual imports ranging from $7.5 billion to $12 billion between the end of the previous trade war in 2020 and 2024.

However, a resumption of Chinese LNG imports would not immediately translate into a major new windfall for US LNG producers.

Although Chinese imports of US LNG halted after the tariffs were imposed, Chinese buyers have continued to honour long-term contracts with US suppliers, purchasing the cargoes and then reselling them elsewhere.

China could also make a relatively straightforward move by lowering duties on US agricultural imports, potentially creating room for Washington to point to increased access for American farmers.

For Trump, such announcements could have particular political value.

He will be looking for tangible trade wins before the midterms, including high-profile purchases of US agricultural products and Boeing aircraft.

Sources told Reuters this month that Xi is preparing a large business delegation to accompany him, similar to his 2015 visit.

During that trip, China signed a $38 billion agreement for 300 Boeing aircraft.

China said after the May summit that it would buy 200 additional Boeing jets, while Boeing described that order as only an "initial tranche" of a potentially much larger transaction.

Beijing and Boeing have remained in prolonged negotiations over a deal that industry sources say could involve 500 737 MAX jets as well as dozens of wide-body aircraft.

The transaction has been stalled for years as Trump has threatened to restrict China's access to critical spare engine parts.

A major Boeing order would therefore offer Trump a high-profile example of US exports benefiting from his negotiations with Beijing, while giving China an opportunity to demonstrate progress on its economic priorities.

Technology and rare earths remain sticking points

The two sides are also expected to negotiate over technology restrictions and critical minerals.

Beijing has been pressing Washington to delay a rule that would prevent thousands of Chinese companies from accessing advanced US technology.

Washington, meanwhile, wants China to ease restrictions on shipments of rare earths and critical minerals that are essential to high-tech industries ranging from automobiles and aerospace to defence.

The issue highlights the increasingly interconnected nature of the US-China relationship.

While Washington wants to limit China's access to technologies considered strategically sensitive, US manufacturers remain dependent on supply chains involving Chinese minerals and processing capacity.

That creates incentives for both sides to negotiate, but also leaves significant room for disagreements over national security and industrial policy.

Taiwan poses a bigger geopolitical risk

Trade may produce the most visible announcements from the summit, but Taiwan could be the most sensitive issue.

US allies in Asia are increasingly concerned that Trump could soften Washington’s support for Taiwan in pursuit of economic agreements with Beijing.

Taiwan rejects China's sovereignty claims over the island.

The US, like most countries, does not maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan, but remains its most important international backer and arms supplier.

Xi is expected to press Trump on Taiwan during the summit. Any change in Washington’s language could be closely scrutinised by governments across Asia.

"There's a great deal of trepidation, particularly from our allies, about where our China policy is going to land," said Emma Chanlett-Avery, political-security affairs director for US-based think tank Asia Society Policy Institute in an earlier Reuters report.

"Any indication of a softness on Taiwan would be quite alarming," she added.

Trump said Xi raised US arms sales to Taiwan during their May meeting.

Trump later described a pending weapons package worth as much as $14 billion as a "negotiating chip".

Beijing is also seeking a change in Washington's longstanding formulation on Taiwan.

People familiar with Chinese efforts told Reuters that Beijing hopes Trump will publicly state that the US opposes Taiwan's independence rather than simply saying Washington does not support independence.

The distinction could carry significant diplomatic weight, particularly for US allies that rely on Washington’s existing position as part of the regional security framework.

Iran adds another layer to the talks

The war in Iran creates another area of potential tension.

Trump is expected to ask Xi to use China's influence with Tehran to curb support for Iran.

China maintains close relations with Tehran and is by far the world's largest buyer of Iranian oil exports, giving Beijing an economic relationship with Iran that Washington believes could provide leverage.

China, however, has shown little inclination to use that influence in line with US demands.

Reuters reported last month that Beijing was selling billions of dollars' worth of goods to Iran through a sanctions-evasion scheme.

China's foreign ministry said it was not aware of such a scheme.

Washington has so far avoided directly targeting Chinese banks as part of its Iran pressure campaign.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stopped short of imposing penalties on Chinese banks when he unveiled an "economic onslaught" against Iran last month and warned countries to cut business ties with Tehran.

"To date, the American President seems content with China’s limited role, saying that the Chinese President had “behaved reasonably well.” This perceived restraint may not stem from Trump’s requests, but rather from Beijing’s calculus in maintaining ties with Gulf partners, including Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates," Toomas Hanso, junior research fellow at the International Centre for Defence and Security, said.

The Iran issue therefore gives Trump another reason to seek cooperation from Beijing, even as the two countries remain strategic competitors.

AI emerges as a new summit issue

Artificial intelligence is also expected to feature prominently when the leaders meet.

The highly anticipated Sept. 24 summit comes as some in the AI industry are calling for greater safeguards around the rapid development of advanced models.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon plan to attend next week's state dinner with Trump and Xi, four people familiar with the event told POLITICO.

Their presence underscores the increasingly strategic role of AI in US-China relations.

Advanced AI models have implications not only for commercial competition but also for national security, military capabilities and control over critical technologies.

Analysts see AI as a potential area for cooperation because both countries face concerns over misuse and the broader risks created by rapidly advancing systems.

But the intense technological competition between Washington and Beijing is likely to limit the scope for substantive cooperation.

Any agreement on AI safeguards could therefore be largely symbolic, particularly as both countries continue to compete over chips, computing infrastructure, advanced models and access to the technologies needed to build them, Reuters said.

data.title: Invezz Explains: India wants UPI revenue but its payment data may be worth more
data.description:
India’s decision to introduce a merchant discount rate on selected UPI payments has reopened a debate over who should pay for the country’s digital payment infrastructure.

From October 15, person-to-merchant transactions above ₹2,000 will attract an MDR of 0.4%, capped at ₹300, while person-to-person transfers, smaller payments and small merchants remain protected.

The government says about 96% of merchant transactions will remain unaffected.

But the bigger question sits beyond the fee itself. UPI is not only a payments rail, but it is also creating digital transaction records that can help formalise businesses, improve credit assessment and give lenders a clearer view of cash flows.

That raises another question: as India starts monetising UPI directly, could the data generated by the network ultimately be worth more than the MDR revenue?

UPI’s value is no longer just in moving money

The scale is enormous. UPI processed 24.5 billion transactions worth about ₹29.82 lakh crore in August, according to NPCI data.

For banks and fintechs, a payment can have value beyond the few basis points earned for processing it.

Key takeaway

A reliable digital trail can show how frequently a merchant receives money, how stable those inflows are and whether sales are growing.

Indian policymakers have recognised this. Government material on digital public infrastructure says UPI has helped small businesses establish verifiable transaction histories, improving the ability of banks and fintechs to assess creditworthiness.

That does not mean UPI transaction data can simply be sold or repurposed. Lending and data-sharing remain subject to consent, privacy and regulatory safeguards.

But the financial footprint created by digital payments can become an underwriting input when accessed lawfully.

That matters in India, where many small businesses have historically lacked the financial records lenders prefer.

MDR solves one problem but could create another

The case for MDR is straightforward, as UPI costs money to operate.

Professor Ashish Das of IIT Bombay told Invezz that the network has a real operating cost.

“There is a cost for running the UPI system. The approximate cost can run into several thousand crores,” Das said.

He estimated annual costs could fall between ₹5,000 crore and ₹20,000 crore, while the new MDR system could generate roughly ₹15,000 crore. Those are estimates rather than audited figures, but they illustrate the funding problem.

Das said the economics depend on how closely MDR revenue matches the actual cost of running UPI. If revenue exceeds that cost, the system creates a profit pool; if it falls short, the funding gap remains.

ASSOCHAM President Nirmal K Minda told Invezz that MDR would make UPI more sustainable and support investment in infrastructure, fraud prevention and innovation.

Jyoti Prakash Gadia, managing director of Resurgent India, made a similar argument, saying the revenue could help banks and payment providers fund cybersecurity and expansion, although it may not fully recover investments already made in building UPI.

The hidden risk is losing valuable digital behaviour

The tension begins if merchants respond to MDR by changing behaviour.

Dr Manoranjan Sharma, chief economist at Infomerics Ratings, told Invezz that the legal incidence of the charge and its economic incidence need not be the same.

Merchants could absorb the cost, but they could also reduce discounts, raise prices or steer customers towards other payment methods. Sharma said consumers should watch for cash discounts, altered pricing and payment-specific incentives.

“If merchants raise broad prices rather than visibly charging UPI users, MDR becomes part of general operating costs and consumers may not identify its source,” he said.

Key takeaway

The bigger economic risk would emerge if some merchants shifted transaction volume back towards cash.

Previous government policy promoted low-value UPI partly because digital payments formalise transactions and create financial footprints that can improve access to credit.

A cash transaction produces far less usable information for a lender assessing business activity.

That makes the trade-off more complicated than MDR revenue versus merchant costs. India could gain a recurring source of funding for its payments network while weakening, at the margin, the data trail that makes the network useful for lending and formalisation.

The real prize may sit beyond payments

The new MDR framework does not necessarily undermine UPI’s data advantage. Most transactions remain outside the charge, and small merchants retain protections.

But policymakers now have two objectives to balance.

UPI needs sustainable economics for banks, apps and payment providers. It also needs merchants to keep choosing digital payments often enough for their transaction histories to remain useful.

Gadia told Invezz that the central challenge is ensuring higher ecosystem costs do not ultimately translate into higher consumer costs.

The same logic applies to data.

Key takeaway

The ₹15,000-crore revenue opportunity is visible and immediate. The value of millions of businesses building long-term digital financial histories is harder to put on a balance sheet.

For India, that less visible asset may ultimately prove more important.

data.title: SpaceX stock forecast after hitting a $946 million NASA deal
data.description:
SpaceX stock has moved sideways at an important price, even after the company received a $964 million deal by NASA. SPCX also wavered as investors waited for the upcoming Starship Orbital test. It trades at $152, up by 47% from its lowest level this year. 

SpaceX stock wavers after reaching a NASA deal

SPCX stock wavered even after the company reached a big deal with NASA. In a statement, the agency awarded it three additional missions through a contract modification. 

The extension, worth about $946 million, will bring the number of missions to 17, and will help it maintain access to the space station. This amount includes ground, launch, in-orbit, and return and recovery operations. The total contract in this program is worth $5.92 billion.

SpaceX is seeing strong growth in its launch business. In its last earnings report, the company said that its space business brought in over $962 million in revenues, up from $746 million in the same period last year. 

The new contract comes as the company prepares to conduct its major Starship test on September 28. This test was initially scheduled for September 22nd, before it was moved to a later date. 

Elon Musk hopes that the new Starship will take the third version of its Starlink satellites in space. The new version will have 10x more capacity than the current one, allowing more speeds for end users. It will help it compete further with telecommunication companies like T-Mobile and AT&T. In a statement, Elon Musk said:

“Even if our monetization per bit dropped by a factor of 10, that would still mean a 10x increase in the revenue of Starlink. I think people are really underestimating Starlink here. This is a big deal.”

Starlink is the biggest cash earner for SpaceX. In its last earnings report, the company said that the connectivity business made over $4.29 billion, up sharply from the $3.2 billion it made last year. Its number of customers jumped to over 12 million, and the trajectory is accelerating. 

READ MORE: SpaceX stock outlook: where will SPCX be in the next five years?

SpaceX is becoming a big data center player

SPCX stock is also benefiting from the ongoing artificial intelligence boom. It runs Grok, a popular chatbot, and a large data center operation. It moved into the cloud services business, by providing access to its Colossus and Colossus II sites in the second quarter. This business contributed $1.6 billion in incremental revenue in the quarter. 

Most notably, the company continues to ramp up its data center operations and has already received some major orders. For example, the company recently inked a $1.1 billion-a-month deal with an unnamed client. It also received orders from companies like Anthropic, Google, and Reflection AI. 

This business explains why analysts believe that its revenue will continue growing in the near term. The average estimate is that its revenue will cross $150 billion next year, much higher than the $18 billion it made last year.

SpaceX stock price technical analysis

SPCX stock chart | Source: TradingView

The two-hour chart shows that the SPCX stock has soared in the past few weeks. It jumped from a low of $104.60 in August to the current $153. 

The stock formed an ascending triangle pattern, a common continuation sign in technical analysis. It has remained above the 50-period moving average. 

Therefore, the stock will have a bullish breakout, potentially to the next key level at $200.

data.title: Dow closes 110 pts lower as treasury yields rise and oil stays above $100
data.description:
US stocks ended mixed on Friday as investors wrapped up a volatile week marked by the Federal Reserve’s first interest-rate hike in three years, rising Treasury yields and elevated oil prices.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 114.74 points, or 0.22%, to 51,663.30, while the S&P 500 gained 11.53 points, or 0.12%, to 7,647.19.

The Nasdaq Composite advanced 92.72 points, or 0.35%, to 26,511.01.

The moves came as investors assessed the potential impact of a higher-for-longer interest-rate environment on equities and fixed-income markets. A semiconductor rally helped limit the pressure on broader US equities.

Treasury yields remain elevated

Treasury yields moved higher on Friday, adding to pressure on stocks.

The 10-year Treasury yield briefly climbed back above 5% after retreating on Thursday and was last up more than five basis points at 4.998%.

The benchmark yield had already risen above 5% earlier in the week, reaching its highest level since July 2007.

The move has kept inflation and interest-rate expectations in focus as investors assess the Federal Reserve’s next steps.

The Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points this week, taking the target range to 3.75%-4%.

Markets are now pricing in more than a 50% probability of another rate increase at the central bank’s October meeting, up from 42.5% a week earlier and 7.2% a month ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

The prospect of additional rate increases could keep pressure on Treasury yields in the coming months.

Oil remains above $100 a barrel

Oil prices retreated on Friday but remained above $100 a barrel, keeping inflation concerns elevated.

West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 1.58% to settle at $100.30 a barrel, while Brent crude futures declined 0.91% to close at $103.87.

Crude prices eased from session highs after China, at Saudi Arabia’s request, asked Iran to limit attacks by Houthi rebels on Saudi oil infrastructure.

However, oil remained at levels that could add to broader inflationary pressures.

Soaring oil prices have also pushed US diesel prices to record levels, potentially increasing costs across farming and shipping.

The combination of elevated oil prices and rising bond yields has added to concerns about the outlook for inflation and monetary policy.

Dow posts third weekly decline

Friday’s session ended the major indices on a mixed week. The Dow was down nearly 2% for the week, posting a third consecutive weekly decline and its worst weekly performance since March.

The S&P 500 was down 0.3% week to date, while the Nasdaq was up 0.3%, making it the only major index on track for a weekly gain.

Investors also monitored company-specific developments.

Berkshire Hathaway announced that Warren Buffett will step down as chairman and become chairman emeritus, nine months after handing the CEO role to Greg Abel.

Xenon Pharmaceuticals fell after temporarily pausing enrollment in clinical studies of an experimental drug following reports of side effects.

Cryptocurrency-linked stocks including Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood surged as Bitcoin prices jumped.

The quarterly expiry of stock and index derivatives, known as triple witching, also contributed to late-session volatility.

data.title: Accenture stock falls 4% today: here's why
data.description:
Accenture (ACN) stock fell 4% on Friday after Guggenheim downgraded the consulting and technology services company to Neutral from Buy and removed its previous price target.

The downgrade came as Guggenheim said its channel checks had not identified a corresponding improvement in demand despite Accenture shares rebounding 52% from their June lows.

The firm also pointed to job-posting data showing fewer openings and Accenture's recent push into the mid-market through the launch of Accenture Edge.

Guggenheim interpreted the move as an indication that demand from core enterprise customers remains challenged.

Despite the 52% gain from June, ACN stock is down 29% in 2026.

Analysts see limited improvement in demand

Guggenheim's downgrade adds to a mixed view among Wall Street analysts.

According to TipRanks data provided in the source, seven of 18 analysts have a Buy rating on Accenture, while 11 have a Hold rating.

Deutsche Bank also highlighted weak demand trends but took a different approach to its price target. The bank raised its target for Accenture to $175 from $136 while maintaining a Hold rating ahead of the company's fiscal fourth-quarter earnings report.

Deutsche Bank attributed the higher target primarily to increased valuations among peer companies.

However, the bank's assessment of Accenture's underlying demand remained cautious.

The analyst said there was no discernible evidence of a rebound in spending and argued that AI-related investment remains concentrated in a limited number of use cases.

According to Deutsche Bank, that investment has yet to translate into higher budgets for traditional IT services.

Accenture's scale supports its business

Accenture remains a major player in technology consulting and professional services.

The company serves roughly 9,000 clients across more than 120 countries, providing strategy and technology services.

Its FY 2025 annual report highlighted a digital transformation partnership with UniCredit aimed at modernising technology across 13 European markets.

Accenture also reported that it has worked with 195 of its 200 largest clients for more than a decade, a relationship that supports long-term client retention.

For fiscal 2025, revenue reached nearly $69.7 billion, an increase of approximately 7.4% from the previous year. Net income was around $7.8 billion.

Revenue has also increased from approximately $64.1 billion in fiscal 2023, reflecting growth in the company's business over that period.

Balance sheet and competitive challenges

Accenture's financial position provides another part of the investment picture.

Based on its August 2025 balance sheet, the company had a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.3x and a current ratio of nearly 1.4x.

The company also generated close to $10.9 billion in free cash flow, representing cash remaining after operating expenses and capital investments.

However, Accenture faces competition from large technology companies as well as newer businesses focused on artificial intelligence.

Its reliance on ecosystem partners for a significant portion of revenue also creates potential risks if those partners develop competing offerings.

Regulatory developments could add another challenge. Regulations such as the EU AI Act could require additional compliance spending and operational changes.

Geopolitical tensions may also make it more difficult for Accenture to forecast demand for consulting services.

With shares having recovered significantly since June while analysts continue to flag soft demand, the company's fiscal fourth-quarter results will provide investors with another indication of how enterprise technology spending is developing.
